utterances.text: It somehow happened that in the case of the first shell, some information came up; namely, that the shell had arrived from Poljine, a Serb position there. Was that plausible or was that determined exactly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was probably a report of one of the crime inspectors. In the ballistic reports, we did not refer to exact positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. I know that in one incident, UNPROFOR wrote that it came from the area between Brijeg and somewhere else. I think that was written up in the case of one of these incidents in Livanjsko. Again, that did not affect us. We did not accept that as some kind of a guide-line that we would include in our own report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this photograph be admitted, if it's not already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D739, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D02250. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that this is from UNPROFOR? This doesn't seem to be right. I think it should be turned differently. I see. Do you remember -- actually, do you see that on this map, they provided firing tables, Yugoslav ones? Did you persuade them to do that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably when I gave them the rules for 82-millimetre mortars, they probably did it that way. But I'm telling you, once again, this is the first time I see this map. They were not duty-bound to show their reports to us, nor did they want to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, though, that this is a table for Yugoslav charges and that this map pertains to that incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can assume that. Perhaps it's been taken out of context here. I do not know this off the top of my head. I did this work 16 years ago. As for ranges and charges for this mortar, with this angle of descent, it could be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the apex? That is Kosevsko Brdo or something like that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. The apex is the apex of that angle. I don't know. We can only zoom in the map of the city, but let us think that this is Kosevsko Brdo. However, if you could zoom in, then I would be more certain that it is Kosevsko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the city and then Kosevsko Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D740, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that according to the official report, in this incident the azimuth from the east was 20 -- or, rather, from the north it was 70, which makes up a total of 90, right, and in this report what is referred to is that the possible point from where the firing took place is in the broader area of Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I would request that the witness be shown the report if he's to be asked detailed questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. 65 ter 13331.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that we had established that the Presidency had asked Mr. Miokovic to hand in his report the same evening, the same day?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We read that a few moments ago in his report, that the Presidency had requested that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that they did not wait for your findings, and they didn't inform you about it either; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've already established that too. They didn't wait, and they didn't inform us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at page 6. We have both in English, actually. Can we have one in Serbian for the interpreters. Yes, that is page 6 of the document and page 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask you to cast a glance at this report. It would be good thing if the other participants could see this page. It's probably the last page or the penultimate one with the signature of Mr. Miokovic.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this report in the case of General Milosevic, and there was this discussion to the effect that our ballistic report did not correspond with this one. It wasn't 20 degrees from the east, but from the north. I would like us to have a look at our report. This confirms that Miokovic handed in this report without waiting for us to complete our part of the job and without waiting for our findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that the way he usually acted or was he forced to hand in his report on the same day? If it's not easy for you to answer that question, you don't have to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll give you an answer, stating that I don't know. You will have to ask him. Miokovic and the other members of the Centre of the Security Services, in practice, of course, usually waited for our findings to complete their report. Now, why he did it this way in this particular case, you will really have to ask him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted, unless it's already been admitted on some other basis?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this has been admitted as Exhibit P1706.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The 65 ter number is 13331?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let's look at this report from the on-site investigation. It says that the azimuth is 15 from the north --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: From the east, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- and 75 from the south.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just a moment, let's look at the page. It's the same document. 431 is the end of the ERN number. Page 8, page 8. Yes, this is it in Serbian. Can we have it in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember -- do you agree that it says here: "15 towards the north-east, calibre 82 millimetres"? So how can someone determine the azimuth according to the north-east, rather than the north? Do you agree that this is rather unusual?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that it's unusual, and I would like to see the ballistics report that we drew up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we seeing the correct English page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think it should be the third page in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "On November --" or "8th of November," description point 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are forensic technicians a different service from the Ballistic Service or are they one-and-the-same service?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation. They were, in fact, the technical support for the ballistics experts, so it was their duty to wait for the ballistics experts and consult them before entering any conclusions into the report. So I can comment on this as being an error, an omission on the side of the forensic technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the case of General Milosevic, there was a certain change in the angle. Here is what it says in the judgement in that case, the last few sentences. It refers to you and the Higgs experts who interpreted this to be south-east, and 1.658, the conclusions of both --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Another Chamber's finding has nothing to do with us in this trial. Move on to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, but evidently there were many misunderstandings stemming from this facile determination of angles by a person who was not authorised to do this and who didn't know how to do it. So let's now move on from the topic of Livanjska Street and deal with something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the incident in Dobrinja of the 4th of February, 1994, a day before Markale? It's in Attachment G, incident number 7.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the queue for humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was one day before Markale 1, as we call that incident; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a day before Markale 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at a map of Dobrinja and point to the place?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D02151.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this map sufficient for you to mark the place where the queue for humanitarian aid was and where the incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't use this map to do that. Dobrinja is quite a complicated place, as far as I'm concerned. I would like to see our reports and our map and the sketch of the site. This is all well documented. Here, I can't see the names of all the streets. I don't know exactly what part of Dobrinja this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So let's try with a different map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D02191.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's on a larger scale, so is it easier for you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to recall exactly what street this was in, and then I could mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was in the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. The number of the street is 353, because we're -- it's impossible to write the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that is true, then this would be the street, 353. But I don't know whether it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Before we continue, the witness has already requested to see the reports of the incident before he makes a marking. He hasn't had the opportunity to review the evidence concerning this specific incident. He's been asked to pick one of very many incidents in respect of which he participated in an investigation. My request is that Mr. Karadzic put to the witness the reports relating to this before asking him to mark the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll come to a similar situation. Do you have a compilation of his investigation report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This specific incident wasn't in his amalgamated statement, but we can get the report relating to this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It would be beneficial for the witness to have his report in front of him, if possible. Do you have the 65 ter number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 65 ter 09617. And certainly I will be very happy to jog the witness's memory. Can we now have 65 ter 09617, and then we'll come back to this map when Mr. Sabljica recalls these geographic relations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It used to be called Jawaharlal Nehru Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I grew up in the city center, and I'm not familiar with Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have the Serbian version? Oh, yes, yes. Can we have page 12 of this document. We need page 12. 794 should be the last three digits of the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at this page, please, and familiarise yourself with it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading it right now. Does this set contain the ballistics report I signed, because this is a report on the forensic inspection of the site by the forensic technicians?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, but there are photographs also. Could we have a hard copy of this document? That would be excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's a 92-page document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have page 15, and then 16, to see if that will assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is better, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, please look at this page, and then we'll continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is a translation, it would be useful to have it, for the sake of the other participants, so we don't need to waste time reading aloud, for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember this landed on a field near the public parking-lot in Mihajlo Pupin Street.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please? Is there an English translation of this document so we don't have to read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we established that it had arrived from the east, and there was an Energoinvest building there, or, rather, a group of buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You determined the direction, but you did not specify the place from which it was fired?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We only mentioned a facility that was there, the Energoinvest building, but these were just landmarks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we show page 4 in English and page 20 in B/C/S so that the witness can familiarise himself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's just where we were heading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can show just the B/C/S version only. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You can see Oslobodilaca Grada Street, the public garage, the asphalt parking-lot, and the markings 1 and 2, where the shells landed, and S, which stands for "North" in our language. So "S" means "North."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Two shells are marked here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think the third one landed on a house of worship, in a room somewhere, so we from ballistics did not investigate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And we have number 3 here in the right-hand column?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the third one. I think the judge was Zdenko Eterovic who attended the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have the next page. I think it will be of even greater assistance to you. So the next page, 21, please. Can we have 1D09048, which is a Google photograph of the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did the 1D number reach 9000 already? I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 02148, 1D02148. As this is a Google photograph of the area, it would probably assist Mr. Sabljica to mark those places. One is enough. Let's have the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise what is on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the parking-lot of Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. I don't know exactly what street this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is very important for us, Mr. Sabljica, because there is some confusion about the address and the place in the reports. The street on which these two cars can be seen in front of the parking-lot, what street is this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a street leading from Dobrinja towards Lukavica. I think a trolley bus runs down this street, but that's not the same part of town. That's not the same neighbourhood as the one we were referring to. I don't think this photograph corresponds to the site where the shells landed. This is in the upper part of Dobrinja, near the main road from the federation -- leading between the federation and Republika Srpska, in the direction of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the drawing we had, and we can look for it again, does it correspond to this? Are there two such places in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't think this is the same place. I think it's a bit below this area. It's not as close to the main road as shown here. It's closer to Dobrinja 4. You could see, in the earlier map that you showed me, where the Branilaca Sarajeva Street is. In the lower part of the Dobrinja settlement, if we look at all of the different neighbourhoods from 1 to 4, it is in the area marked with "353," whereas the upper portions of Dobrinja, near the main road with a trolley line towards Eastern Sarajevo, is, that's where it is. That's what we see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then we have to go back to the map again. Maybe if we look at it now, it will be easier for you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll try to pin-point the area on that map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then please have 1D02191 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can this assist you, the Lukavica road that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see the upper portion of this map. Can you see that? That means that that aerial photo was from the upper quadrant, whereas 353 indicates the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now please mark the street 353 with a pen there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you zoom out again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Well, here it is, 353. This is the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. I can put an OS there, if you like [marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see, very well, OS. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, please -- could you please show where Mihajla Pupina Street is on this map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the street right here [marks], MP, "Mihajlo Pupin," and I believe that the incident was someplace around here [marks]. That's all I can conclude from this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mihajla Pupina Street was renamed, and it is now Zlatni Ljiljan Street; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know what the new names are in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the "466" number that you see there? Is that the Josip Marsala Sosa [phoen] Square; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, we see up here "Lukavicka Cesta," "Lukavica Road," and below is the road leading from Dobrinja to the airport. Do you know what its name is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the name of that street, but I have -- I have a general idea where the street is, but I really don't know what its name is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, could you please draw a line here on this map, the separation line?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean between the two armies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Would you agree with me that this is the airport neighbourhood where it says "Luja Pastera Street," and so on, that this was under the control -- Serbian control?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that. I don't know. It wasn't under Serbian control, under the control of the Republika Srpska Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw the separation line here? Can you show it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I will make an approximation, but I'm not very familiar with Dobrinja. So I believe it would run this way, approximately, and then towards outward, as far as I can tell on this map, because I am for sure this is the church at Meljine, and that was for sure under the control of the Republika Srpska Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate the airport, where that is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here, I'll put an A for it [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now please put number 1 at the incident site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this map, can you indicate the direction of Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. It's eastward here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you indicate Hamdije Kapidzica Street? That was the Jawaharlal Nehru Street earlier, but now it's Hamdije Kapidzica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here it is [marks]. I'll put an H there [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but we can also see that it's already entered there. Would you agree with me that there was a police station building on this street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean is there a police station now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, then.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really confirm that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will show another document later. But before you sign this, let me just see if I want you to mark anything else here. Can you tell us -- can you tell us something about the incident site and Hamdije Kapidzica Street and their mutual relation is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they are very close, one to the other, relatively speaking, if you look at the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please date this map and sign it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Here it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we -- I'd like to tender this, please, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D741, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note the time, Mr. Karadzic. Do you have some questions until 12.00?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. I think then we better go on break, and then I'll continue when we come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I think -- my recollection is it was a confidential matter between the parties, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Mr. Tieger, albeit we have the curtains drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought I made it clear this was supposed to be in private session, and I understood we would be beginning that way. My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I would ask for an appropriate redaction as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And thank you, Your Honour, for noting that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for the witness to be brought in again: With respect to your request for leave to reply to Mr. Karadzic's response to bar table motion regarding Mr. Thomas' testimony, since we find that it would be helpful, we grant it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And if I may raise one other matter, a scheduling matter. Projecting out the schedule for the remainder of the week, based on today's revision, it would appear that the last witness, Mr. Hamill, would not complete his testimony this week and then would have to either have an extended stay or return after the testimony of Witness Fraser [phoen], whose dates are fixed for the following week. With that in mind, the Prosecution would ask if the Court could consider the possibility of further sessions this week that might complete the witness's testimony this week, as anticipated earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll consider that, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just to confirm, we have another witness before Mr. John Hamill, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one observation from our part. We think it would be wiser for the Prosecution to tell Mr. Hamill not to come this week, and that way he won't be inconvenienced. Because if you do the math, I don't think there would be much time on Thursday for him to even begin his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's appreciated, Your Honour, but it's too late for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now establish where and what happened, exactly where?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter 09617.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That has been entered as Exhibit P1710, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 18, please, and let us see how the investigation was conducted in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This report was prepared by a forensic technician. We don't have to mention his name. You can read it on the document, itself. You see his name; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He was a criminal technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us what it says underneath this line, "Description of incident"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Subject: Shelling." And the site is Dobrinja, down-town Sarajevo. And the date is 4th February 1995 [as interpreted] as the date of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that street exist, to the best of your knowledge, in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The street that does exist is, as we've already seen, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The transcript should read "1994."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us now see what it says here where this actually happened. Could we now have the same document, page 12, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it appear, when one sees an error of this type, that a person actually drew up the report without ever actually going on site, when he makes an error such as naming the wrong street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this specific case, I know that this gentleman did go out to the site. But as for why he made this error in the street name, you have to ask him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, please, with number 2 there, what does it say under number 2?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Place and time." And then it says: "Dobrinja, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street." And then underneath, it says: "Nehru Street." Probably Jawaharlal Nehru, the earlier street name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that's probably the old name for the street, right, the Nehru Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please bear with me a moment. Could we now please have 1D02191 again on the screens. My apologies, 1D02182. 1D02182.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at the third name from the bottom. To the left -- on the left-hand side, we see the old name, and then on the right-hand side, we have the new names. Could you please read that out?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It says, on the left, "Dzevaharlal Nehrua," and on the right-hand side it says "Hamdije Kapidzica Street."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember marking Hamdije Kapidzica Street, and that, in fact, it was a whole block away from the playground, that there was -- intervening between the sites there was a block of buildings; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have -- or, actually, I'd like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What document are you referring to, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The list of street names, the old and new names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who compiled it? Who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this was from Adobe Reader that I got it from, but we have a lot of evidence showing that is correct. Well, this was actually a city plan that was used to get these names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. For the moment, we don't accept that this is a genuine list of the new and old names. We would need to verify that. Mr. Karadzic has still not provided any information as to the underlying basis for the list of new and old names. So for the record, we don't accept it as accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We're not satisfied as to its foundation at this moment, Mr. Karadzic, so it's difficult for us to admit it at this stage. At best, we can mark it for identification, but you would still need to bring the witness to give the foundation evidence in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Well, this was the city plan for the city of Sarajevo, issued by -- published by Slovenes. And on the back of the plan, there is a whole list of new and old names. But we will get this other document in a moment. Could we now please see again -- well, can we just MFI this document, and then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would rather not produce as many MFI documents. Why don't we wait.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that we now have the original document. Can I please ask the Usher's assistance. Well, let me just take a look at it, and then we will show it to the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber, and then we will ask the witness to actually identify this city plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on. You can do it tomorrow, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I just -- can I just interrupt to request that we provided a copy of that map. I don't believe it was on the list that's been released to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we can deal with all that tomorrow. Now, can we please pull again 1D02191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or Exhibit D741 on which the witness marked.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we can use that one as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, we can use this map as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, could you please indicate 353 again, mark it here. That's the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now we have it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have it, so we can use this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now please tell us, sir, whether this street ends at Mimar Sinana Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, it does not intersect with Hamdije Kapidzica Street, but, rather, between Mimar Sinana Boulevard and Hamdije Kapidzica Street, there is a small street connecting indicated with 228 on the map; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please now mark on this map the -- indicate where the north is? Could you indicate the bearing, the north bearing, parallel to Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately it's in this direction [marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please re-admit this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can just keep this exhibit as marked currently.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we save it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that can be done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see the sketch again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you still feel that the Google depiction was not very helpful?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, because it only showed the quadrant of Dobrinja in the direction of Lukavicka Street.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, then we'll move on to something else. Can we have 65 ter 09617, page 23, please. That's a document we've already seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 09617, page 19. So it's the same document, but page 19. Page 20, yes, page 20, a sketch of the scene. It's probably 19, what we see now. We need a sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw a line in the middle of the street Oslobodilaca Grada?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we pull out page 4 of the English. That's more convenient for everybody. Could you wait. Ignore this one. We pull up page 4 of the English. Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the street Oslobodilaca Grada, can you please draw a line there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you write a number there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Say number 1 [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see that it says "Oslobodilaca Grada" here as well; it doesn't say "Oslobodilaca Sarajeva"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now indicate to us how the north was marked here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is it, north.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that differ from what it is like on the map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as I look at this, this is a different depiction of the scene. If we would turn it in the direction in which it is on the map, it would be no difference, because this street has to be 180 degrees this way [indicates], it has to be rotated, and then we'd have the same situation like on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 180 degrees?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then it would be moving from east to west; right? Is the north marked vertical in relation to this street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that differ from what we saw there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is something wrong here, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously this sketch is not exactly very precise, and it is hard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Why don't we keep this. Could you put the date and your signature here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll keep this. In the meantime, can we bring the map which we saw a minute ago at the same time, which is D741, so that the witness can compare those two pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll give a separate number for this marked sketch.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the sketch will be Exhibit D742.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then we'll compare the two documents, D741 and D742.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that the technical people have understood this. We need to have this marked, one on half of the screen, and on the other half of the screen we should have the map, if I understood things correctly. Is there any doubt in the minds of the technical people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's coming. It takes some time, Mr. Karadzic. Now, do you understand the crux of the question, Mr. Sabljica? Can you answer the question again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. The street Oslobodilaca Sarajeva is this street over here [indicates]. 353, it is marked here. I did not mark the north right. I think that it should be a bit perpendicular to this street, if we are going to go by this sketch, which is more precise than what I drew on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You think that what you marked on the map is wrong and that the sketch is right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the sketch is right, because this is the first time I saw the map. I tried to draw the position of Dobrinja in relation to other parts of town and the north, so I approximately marked the north without any measurements, without a compass, without anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is a city map orientated towards the north; that is to say, that the north is on top and the south is on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never drew a city map or a city plan, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So then your sketch -- then your drawing is better than this sketch. We have a city map here. We have to clarify this, because this is one of the drastic mistakes made by these technical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, is it your opinion that you can draw the north direction again on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I were to take this sketch as appropriate and relevant, it is very hard now to do this because I don't know how I'm going to turn the street Oslobodilaca Grada and then the quadrant number 1 where these incidents occurred, where the shells fell. Then we would then have to turn the north on the map perpendicular to 353, if we're going to take the sketch as meritorious. It is very hard to explain -- to compare it to the map. The crime technician made the sketch, and then he drew it rather arbitrarily. It is not that specific and precise. However, in that case, the north was established with the assistance of a compass, whereas on the map, I marked it arbitrarily, rather arbitrarily, without any specific assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we have a black pen, could you mark on this map that you worked on the north that would be at a degree of 90 degrees with 353? And let's see what that would look like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just hold a minute. Can you do that with two pictures at the same time appearing? So we collapse this sketch, and we'll have the Exhibit D741 only. And change the colour into black.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If the sketch were right, can you mark the north for us, then?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like this [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to ask you to look at the city map, the city plan, and to tell us what this looks like on the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be shown to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll keep this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or if the Prosecution prefers some other map where everything can be seen clearly, that is fine. But let us just see the directions in which the streets go. Could I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to cast a glance at this. [In English] Could you please show it -- after the witness, I would like the Chamber to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is the ELMO working? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please go above "Dobrinja," and mark the coordinates, or, rather, the cardinal points, north, south, east, west? Can that be marked? A NATO marking, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like the witness to mark on this original map?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can make a copy during the break. But perhaps now let's do without it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where the north is here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I marked it before with a red arrow on the electronic map, where it says "N," rather than perpendicular to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are a better draftsman than this technician?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seem to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then there's no need to mark this. It is clear that there is a proper orientation for north. It is up on top. Do you agree that there is some angle between the north and Oslobodilaca Sarajeva? Say it's about 30 or 35 degrees?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly that, 35, 30 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Certainly not 90 degrees?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Perhaps we can ask the witness to have a look at the last page and see what it says there under "353," what the name of the street was then. [In English] May I ask you to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you do that? Witness, the accused asked you to take a look at the rear page of the real map and to find out the name of the street at that time, 353.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's a problem for you, we'll get it off Google.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a bit of a problem for me to find it here on this list.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, we'll find something. Can we now have page 23 of this document, 09617.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can safely keep the marking as lastly marked. I refer to Exhibit D741. We'll keep it as lastly marked by the witness, with the black arrow as --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can the witness just confirm that the black arrow, the east, corresponds to the sketch, whereas this corresponds to what the witness confirmed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to correct you. You mean "north," but you did say "east."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean "north."

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the black arrow corresponds to the sketch --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have page 23 of that document, 09617.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry. Perhaps the end of the -- the part that the interpreter did not hear could be repeated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The black arrow corresponds to the "North" on the sketch rather than on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that that is what we need. Now, can we have 65 ter 09617. It's a well-known document. Page 23. Yes, we had it here a few moments ago. Can you show the caption so that Mr. Sabljica can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that what is written here, what is written underneath, underneath this picture -- I mean, this red arrow, does it show the point of impact of one of the shells?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which shell was that, in terms of succession?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard for me to say that on the basis of this picture. I don't know which one it would be, in terms of a succession.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the edge of the playground here in the direction of the pavement or sidewalk? Can you mark the playground with a shadow or something and then the edge of the playground facing the sidewalk?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mark the playground [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excellent, thank you. And now the edge going towards the pavement?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perpendicular to the pavement or parallel to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can mark both.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see that on the playground, there is soil scattered over the playground in the direction from which the projectile arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to conclude, based on this photograph, whether this is a soil or whether this is soot, soot originating from the gunpowder in the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But we can see that this is the place of impact, and we can see that it left some traces; is that right? Whether this is soot or soil, we can see the point of impact and the traces; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that there is some sort of dirt here, to refer to it in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you please put your initials and the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D743.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now go back to that sketch. It's page 19 of this document. I apologise. It's 20, it's page 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the numbers 1, 2 and 3 designate the order in which the shells landed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D742, which is in both languages, D742.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree that this is the order in which the shells landed. We didn't know in what order they had been fired. This is the order in which we investigated the scene. Only the person who fired the projectiles knows in what order they were fired.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we have to go back to page 19. Can we have 19 and 20 on the same page, or, rather, can we see them both together. We have D742, the one in English. And in the other half of the screen, can we have page 19 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that it says here: "Point of impact of a mortar shell, 120 millimetres," and they are numbered 1, 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this doesn't tell us which landed first. It, rather, tells us in what order we dealt with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you did not establish or you were not told or you did not have any information to tell you which landed first? The order in which they landed is not marked? You don't know?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I did not have that information, and it would be very difficult to know that. Only the person who fired the projectiles would know that. It would be hard for witnesses, who heard the shells landing, to conclude in what order they had been fired.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we keep the sketch. And instead of page 19, can we have 65 ter, which is the same document -- just a moment. 971 are the last three digits of the ERN number. Instead of 801, we now need 971. The sketch remains, but the left-hand side of the screen has to be changed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 789, 102-5789. So let's go back a little. 789.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 7. Is it correct? E-court page 7.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 6. The description begins on the previous page, near the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if you agree, this is the record drawn up by the investigating judge, and the judge was Eterovic in this case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A description of the site. If it hasn't been translated, can you read this passage?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A description of site. "The shelling occurred at around 1130 hours, and a total of three shells landed. The first two landed almost simultaneously. One landed near the frame of the window in the basement of the building in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, number 8, destroying two rooms of that ground-floor flat in which part of a mosque had been located in wartime. The stabiliser was not found, nor were pieces of shrapnel found."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 7, the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "And according to the place of impact, the direction was established to be east-south-east, the direction from which the shell arrived. There were no -- no persons were killed, and one child was injured. "The second shell landed in the immediate vicinity of the building in Mihajlo Pupin Street, number 3, on the -- in the backyard, on the concrete under-wall. A stabiliser was found on the spot belonging to a 12-millimetre mortar shell. In the vicinity was the grassy part of a park covered with snow which had turned black from the explosion, and traces of blood can be found as well as one children's shoe. "A few minutes later --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I don't think the interpreters finished the last answer of the -- reading out the paragraph. Could you read again from: "A few minutes later ..."?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "A few minutes later, a third shell landed in the immediate vicinity, near the underground garage. This is a children's playground, bounded by buildings in Smaj Hadzimusic [phoen] Street, Mihajlo Pupin Street and Oslobodilaca Grada Sarajeva Street, and the underground garage. Near the garage and the grassy area, there is an asphalt foot-path, and a part of the stabiliser remained stuck in the asphalt. Nearby, there was several pools of blood, with parts of human tissue, and bags of flour which had burst and been spilled, and a boot torn by a piece of shrapnel."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So number 1 refers to the landing of the third shell, and it landed in the spot marked "1"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the report of the investigating judge, yes, that's how it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact that children remained in the playground even after two shells had landed in the immediate vicinity almost simultaneously?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I explain that? It's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because the children would run away, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Not just children; anyone in the area would flee.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This document has already been admitted. And since we have not made any alterations to it, I need not tender it. Can we now have page 26 of this same document, 9617.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think we need that sketch anymore, Mr. Karadzic. We can collapse it for the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this one of the points of impact? And which one is it, according to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is one of the points of impact, and I think it's number 1, or, rather, the one that's marked as number 1 on the sketch at the edge of the playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the third in order?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be the third one according to the investigating judge's report, but it would be number 1 on our sketch. If you will allow me: The investigating judge took witness statements. He was accompanied by the crime police inspector. We were not concerned with the order in which the shells had been fired. It's hard to conclude when a shell landed and when someone fled. All we did was establish the traces, what the traces were, and that's what we referred to in our report. And as to why the judge did not correct our report, you'll have to ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you first dealt with the first traces you came across and not in the order in which the shells landed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Looking at this photograph, can you mark the longer axis, where the top of the projectile hit?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you want. I'll mark it right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we do that, shall we zoom in, or is it okay to mark it on this picture? Can you do that, Mr. Sabljica? Let us proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you don't need the text anymore, we can zoom in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need the text, but I can mark it like this anyway. I'll just draw a line from the center of the explosion towards the longer side. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the direction of the longer axis [marks]. This is the center of the explosion [marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this was marked in red, it might be more visible, but, well, it can stay like this. Can it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not yet, please. Maybe -- maybe we can use a red pen to make it more visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is the longer axis; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now mark the traces of shrapnel on the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to do it on this photograph, although it's not very good. I will mark both ellipses [marks]. So this is the smaller ellipse and this is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please put the date on this document and sign it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D744.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have page 30 of this document. And we might keep the sketch. Let's have page 30 on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a contemporaneous photograph with snow on the ground; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Based on the traces left by the products of the detonation, can you draw a line in the snow indicating the approximate direction from which the projectile arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a great difficulty, but I will try to do it approximately. I don't see the center here, the point of impact, so I don't know how relevant the markings will be. It will be very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, are the traces of shrapnel on the building of assistance?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you do that, why don't we zoom in further. Once again. Do it once again. We see number 8. What is it, Mr. Sabljica, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 8 indicates some trace evidence. I am not sure. This was probably something that the crime technician put there perhaps to indicate a piece of clothing, or some kind of bag, or whatever. In any case, the technicians had to fix and mark all of the trace evidence found here. I think I also see a number 7, although you can't really see it very well on this photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. As requested, if you could indicate the approximate direction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, here it is [marks]. I will put a "D" for "Direction" and indicate it with this arrow [marks]. This is just approximate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please date and put your signature on this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 1D02561. And if we can have a split screen again and have 1D02560 and then the other half to show 1D02561, that could help Mr. Sabljica to better orientate himself. Could we now please have on the other half 1D02560.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a recent photo. Is this the same building? Can you tell, based on the walls and the texture, and are these the pockmarks left there by shrapnel fragments?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really answer that, because almost all of the buildings look alike there and they were rather damaged by -- after the shelling. So I couldn't really say decisively that this is the same building, because this is a more recent photo. I really can't answer that. I don't want to guess anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you can also not mark these photos in any way; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can't do that, because that wouldn't really be appropriate, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have that sketch, then, again on the monitors, the marked sketch, D742. D742. Can we just enlarge it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now indicate -- on this field, where it says "Asphalt playground," could you please draw a line showing the same direction that you drew earlier on on the photo? And it should be in relation to the right-hand side of this playground. If you need some assistance, maybe we can have the earlier photo again, the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no need. I can actually indicate that [marks]. This sketch is completely misrepresenting everything, so let me just put it this way: This arrow is to indicate the direction from which the shell came, north-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But we know that the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street is -- runs north-west slightly; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but that's what I indicated on this sketch. I don't want to comment on how precise and accurate this sketch is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you then please put, next to number 2, the same thing you did earlier on, so to show the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Well, let's assume -- let's put it this way. I assume that that's how it was, that's where the direction of the projectile was from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we give it a separate number or we can keep it as it's lastly marked?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But can we just keep these markings that the witness made, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll keep the last markings, red markings, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, now about the method of work of these crime technicians. Can you tell us why the polarity of the -- of Planet Earth was changed here? If Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street runs north-west and north-east, is it correct that this direction, the direction that is indicated here, is, in fact, from the south, that it would imply that the shell came from the south?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this sketch, Mr. Karadzic, I couldn't really draw any conclusions, because if you were to do this appropriately, you cannot do it by me just indicating the direction from which the projectile came based on some sketch. If we were to use this sketch, we could draw the conclusion that the projectile had come from any direction. It's very difficult to draw any conclusions on the basis of this method of work. In order to make a more serious and professional expertise of this, it's really not possible based on a sketch of this type, because what we did in our investigations had to do with the actual situation and the actual trace evidence found on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But if the Branilaca Grada Street is -- runs in the direction as shown here, could you please indicate with an arrow where the airport is in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait. We'll bring in the new one, the newly kept D742. It has yet to come. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, before I do that, I will ignore the marking indicating the direction of north, the north bearing. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You just mark it according to the map.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the map, the airport would be in this direction [indicates]. I will mark it with a green arrow and put an A next to it [marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do we need a new number or can it remain as it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think there would be a problem in keeping the same number. So we'll keep --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As it is currently showing, we lost the date. Could you put the date again, kindly, Mr. Sabljica, on this sketch, the 12th of 10 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll keep this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Should I start with a new incident now or are we running short of time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With the indulgence of the interpreters and all the staff -- I inquired of the possibility to go until 2.00, and if it is agreeable to the parties, we'll do so. Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's fine by us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, can you do that? So we have 20 minutes more. I appreciate the kindness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please bear with us. Very well. This document may be removed from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with an incident on the 22nd of January, 1994, at Alipasino Polje, which was G6 on the indictment schedule, Schedule G6? If you have something, you can just use it to refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring to the incident involving children sledding?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please briefly describe what was -- what this incident actually involved?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that three shells landed. Two hit the ground. They were 82. And one, which was a 120-millimetre shell, landed on a building. We did not investigate that one. I and the late Stankov worked on this particular incident, and I think we had established that it had come from Nedzarici, that these shells had come from Nedzarici, from that general direction. That's in brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us anything about when these shells fell and in what order? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean at what time they landed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and how they followed one another, and how much time elapsed between them.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall that. Maybe you can let me read the report. That would help.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please now have 1D02152. That's a city plan showing Alipasino Polje and Dobrinja neighbourhood. One is sufficient. Can we just blow it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, when we take a look at that report, I will ask you about certain things where you needed refreshing your memory. Could you please mark here on this map with numbers 1, 2 and 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you do that: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I would prefer if -- in our submission, again, if the witness is going to be asked very specific questions about an incident in respect of which there is a report - he's already asked to see the report now - in our submission, he should be shown the report before he's asked to mark anything on the map. Mr. Karadzic -- the report is in evidence. Mr. Karadzic has gone straight to the map. I think we should go to the report first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Will you be assisted if you were to see the report, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'd like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's do that, then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we then please have 9609, 9609. Could Mr. Sabljica be shown or be given a hard-copy report so that he can have it with him, and we can work with the maps? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have it, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm just checking if I have an unmarked version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that it is only a two-page document, and it should be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, this is 65 ter 09608, which has been admitted as Exhibit P1698.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that assist you, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this will help me refresh my memory. We can now have the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please now mark, with numbers 1, 2 and 3, the point of impact where these shells landed? Do you remember it was in Cetinjska and Klare Cetkin Streets; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But could we please zoom in on Alipasino Polje, on that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you can use the hard-copy map that you have before you. Maybe that can help.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we have old street names, and I don't know what the new street names are nowadays in the Alipasino Polje area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you do know what streets these were. Is that the "8" symbol that we see there at the eastern part, the eastern "8" symbol, the Klare Cetkin Street and Bosanska Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's about here [indicates]. I can't quite mark the area -- the point of impact where these shells fell, but I will just indicate the general area. If this is Bosanska Street and this is -- so that's Klare Cetkin Street, this, then, should be Cetinjska Street, the street perpendicular [indicates], so it should be in this general area if Bosanska Street is also there [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This area that you marked, is that where all three shells landed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now please indicate, with numbers 1, 2 and 3, the location where they landed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
